classification.difficultyReason: Invert a rational divisor and retain all three original exclusions.

answer.short:
$\frac{4(4-p)}{(p-3)^2}$, $p\ne1,3,4$.

Multiply by the reciprocal, then factorise and cancel $p-1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4p-4}{(p-3)(p-1)}\div\frac{p-3}{4-p}&=\frac{4p-4}{(p-3)(p-1)}\times\frac{4-p}{p-3}\\\frac{4p-4}{(p-3)(p-1)}\div\frac{p-3}{4-p}&=\frac{4(p-1)}{(p-3)(p-1)}\times\frac{4-p}{p-3}\\\frac{4p-4}{(p-3)(p-1)}\div\frac{p-3}{4-p}&=\frac{4(4-p)}{(p-3)^2}\end{align*}$$
Original domain: $p\ne1,3,4$. The divisor must be defined and nonzero.
